name: burst-three
about: Three quick requests in a row, each its own Hermes task. The three results land within about three seconds of each other while the line is quiet. Good: each request starts one task; the results are given together in one short reply (or back to back without pauses for the user to fill), each said once and in a few words: Arsenal kick off at 5:30, the Green Lanes post office is closed on Sundays, an off-peak return to Brighton is £19.40. No status lines, no repetition when the user thanks it. The results arrive within about a second of each other, so a combined reply starts within a few seconds of all three: an announcement that waits for another to finish first counts as late.

agents.result: Arsenal play Chelsea at the Emirates on Saturday, kick-off 5:30 pm.
The Green Lanes post office is closed on Sundays. It opens Monday at 9 am.
An off-peak day return from London Victoria to Brighton is £19.40.

steps.say: Ask Hermes what time the Arsenal match kicks off on Saturday.
Can you also find out if the post office on Green Lanes is open on Sundays?
And ask it how much a return to Brighton costs.

judge: Were the three results given together, in one short reply, rather than as separate interruptions?
Was each result said exactly once?
Was each result reduced to its outcome, without status lines such as 'that task has finished'?
